channel.itunes:summary: Embodied consciousness, synaptic bioenergetics, clinical disorders of consciousness, stroke syndromes, anesthesia dynamics, and living human neurons vs. artificial neural networks.

image.title: Deep Dive: Embodied Consciousness & Neural Computation

item.title: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
item.description: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

item.title: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
item.description: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

item.title: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
item.description: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

item.title: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
item.description: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

item.title: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
item.description: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

item.title: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
item.description: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

item.title: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
item.description: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

item.title: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
item.description: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: When Stroke Steals Words vs. Meaning — Broca's 'Tan,' Sign-Language Aphasia & Inner Silence
item.description: Traces Broca's 1861 autopsy of Leborgne (and 2007 3T MRI re-scanning), Salk Institute ASL stroke dissociations, corollary discharge, and anendophasia.

item.title: Julian Jaynes on Trial — Did Bronze Age Humans Hear Gods Before Inventing 'I'?
item.description: Puts Julian Jaynes's 1976 Bicameral Mind hypothesis on philological and neurobiological trial against Homeric Greek, Middle Kingdom papyri, and corollary-discharge fMRI.

item.title: Ghosts in the Cortical Map — Civil War Phantoms, Penfield's Probe & Mirror Boxes
item.description: From S. Weir Mitchell's Gettysburg amputees and Wilder Penfield's awake cortical mapping to Ramachandran's mirror box, aplasic phantoms, and somatoparaphrenia.

item.title: Seven Seconds of Now — Patient H.M., Clive Wearing & How Memory Stitches Time
item.description: Unpacks Henry Molaison's 1953 medial temporal resection, Brenda Milner's mirror-star dissociation, Clive Wearing's 7-second diary, and hippocampal time cells.

item.title: The Dreaming Brain Unparalyzed — REM Behavior Disorder & Two-Way Lucid Signals
item.description: From Michel Jouvet's pontine atonia switch and Schenck's REM Behavior Disorder alpha-synuclein prodrome to real-time eye-signal dialogues inside verified REM sleep.

item.title: Where Does Pain Actually Live? — Anzio Beachhead, Nav1.7 & Predictive Interoception
item.description: Debates peripheral nociceptive specificity (Nav1.7 SCN9A) vs. top-down insular predictive interoception (Beecher at Anzio, 1995 boot-nail case, naloxone placebo blockade).

item.title: Before the Brain Had a Name — Egyptian Hearts, Aristotle's Radiator & Herophilus
item.description: How humanity spent 2,000 years locating mind in the heart or diaphragm—from Edwin Smith's trauma papyrus to Aristotle, Herophilus in Alexandria, and Galen's laryngeal pig.

item.title: Wine-Dark Seas & Unspeakable Odors — How Language Shapes Color, Smell & Bedside Pain
item.description: From Gladstone's 1858 shock over Homer's color words and Berlin & Kay's hierarchy to Jahai abstract odor vocabulary and cross-cultural bedside pain ideophones.

item.title: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
item.description: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.

item.title: Dream Surgery at Epidaurus — Asclepian Sleep Temples, Sacred Snakes & Placebo Neurobiology
item.description: Walks into the 4th-century BCE abaton at Epidaurus—translating the carved Iamata stelae alongside archaeological scalpels and modern PAG opioid/CB1 imaging.

item.title: Alkaline Lithium Springs & Unchained Asylums — Soranus of Ephesus & Humane Roman Psychiatry
item.description: How Soranus of Ephesus (~100 CE) condemned chains, darkness, and the 'wandering womb' myth while prescribing cognitive rehabilitation and lithium-rich alkaline waters.

item.title: Strasbourg 1518 & the Dancing Plagues — Rye Ergot Alkaloids vs. Mass Motor Contagion
item.description: Debates Claviceps purpurea ergot alkaloid pharmacology vs. famine-and-curse predictive dissociative trance in the July 1518 Strasbourg Dancing Plague.

item.title: Evolved for the Impossible — Bajau 13-Min Divers, Denisovan Sherpas & 13.7 °C Survival
item.description: How genetic evolution (Bajau PDE10A giant spleens, Denisovan Sherpa EPAS1) and Q10 thermodynamics (Anna Bågenholm's 13.7 °C resuscitation) shield the 20W human brain.
